title: ViperQ: Order Flow Pattern Recognition via Auction Market Theory for Reinforcement Learning Trading
abstract: arXiv:2609.13825v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Reinforcement learning trading systems published in the academic literature overwhelmingly rely on price-aggregate state representations (OHLCV bars) or limit-order-book depth features, leaving microstructure pattern theories from the practitioner literature, namely Auction Market Theory and Market Profile, without a peer-reviewed computational instantiation. We present ViperQ, a reinforcement learning system whose state representation is built explicitly from Auction Market Theory primitives: Volume Point of Control, Value Area position, Low Volume Node flags, Cumulative Volume Delta divergence, and tape-velocity signatures, assembled into a 20-dimensional Z-normalised vector. Two Proximal Policy Optimisation agents are trained with a prospect theory-grounded asymmetric reward function that penalises losing holds at a magnitude consistent with Kahneman and Tversky's loss-aversion coefficient. translated_title: ViperQ：基于拍卖市场理论的订单流模式识别强化学习交易
translated_abstract: 学术界发表的强化学习交易系统绝大多数依赖于价格聚合状态表示（OHLCV K线）或限价订单簿深度特征，而来自从业者文献中的微观结构模式理论——即拍卖市场理论（Auction Market Theory）和市场轮廓理论（Market Profile）——尚未有经过同行评审的计算实例化。我们提出了ViperQ，一个强化学习交易系统，其状态表示明确地由拍卖市场理论原语构建：成交量控制点（Volume Point of Control）、价值区域位置（Value Area position）、低成交量节点标志（Low Volume Node flags）、累积成交量Delta背离（Cumulative Volume Delta divergence）以及逐笔成交速度特征（tape-velocity signatures），并组装成一个20维的Z标准化向量。系统使用基于前景理论（Prospect Theory）的非对称奖励函数训练两个近端策略优化（PPO）智能体，该函数以与卡尼曼和特沃斯基损失厌恶系数相一致的幅度惩罚亏损持仓。系统在留出的十二个月数据分区上进行了评估。
tldr: 该论文提出ViperQ系统，首次将从业者领域的拍卖市场理论原语（成交量控制点、价值区域、低成交量节点、累积成交量Delta背离等）显式构建为强化学习状态表示，并结合反映卡尼曼-特沃斯基损失厌恶系数的前景理论非对称奖励函数训练PPO智能体进行交易。
en_tdlr: The paper proposes ViperQ, a reinforcement learning trading system that explicitly builds its state representation from Auction Market Theory primitives (Volume Point of Control, Value Area, Low Volume Nodes, Cumulative Volume Delta divergence), and trains PPO agents with a prospect theory-grounded asymmetric reward function reflecting Kahneman-Tversky loss aversion.
